title: 群作用下局部记录的下降分类
previous_design_failure: The former input supplied a profinite surjection T to S and its kernel pair, so the desired quotient was already h_S and general sheaf descent largely finished the target.

retained: Fixed profinite site, finite jointly surjective covers, and V-valued sheaves.
replaced: Remove the supplied quotient space S, surjection p, and kernel pair.
Supply instead an arbitrary U-small discrete group acting by homeomorphisms on T.
Allow arbitrary Gamma-equivariant sheaf objects E over h_T, not only topological or representable ones.
not_added: No freeness, properness, compactness, or finiteness of Gamma.
No Hausdorff or representable orbit quotient.
No global lifts or continuous choices.

changed_target: Construct the sheaf orbit quotient and classify exactly which equivariant sheaves are pullbacks from it, including morphisms and arbitrary sheaf base change.
terminal_result: The criterion is trivial stabilizer action on every section over every profinite test. The realization is E/Gamma, and its comparison to h_T fiber-product_Q E/Gamma is an isomorphism precisely under that criterion. Quotient and pullback give the full category equivalence.
minimum_acceptable_completion: Sheaf quotient universal property, with correct local representatives/equality.
Necessary and sufficient non-circular descent criterion on the actual sheaf action.
Construction and full morphism correspondence of realizations.
Base-changed quotient and classification for every sheaf B over Q.
alternate_routes: Explicit separated local-orbit presheaf followed by its matching-family sheafification.
Internal action groupoid, effective equivalence relation, and valid topos descent.
Trivial action of the internal isotropy group followed by factorization through the kernel-pair groupoid.

shortest_valid_completion.route: An expert can cite effective descent for topoi after proving that the action factors through the actual local orbit relation exactly when internal stabilizers act trivially. This is a valid concise solution.
shortest_valid_completion.assessment: The complete classification now needs multiple linked facts about local orbit equality, injectivity of the comparison, local surjectivity, and morphisms. Difficulty remains uncalibrated.
shortest_valid_completion.short_counterexample_status: T=* with a nontrivial action only refutes universal descendability; it does not classify all allowed objects or prove base-change compatibility.

proof_dependency_chain: Construct the local orbit relation using finite covers.
Show its quotient presheaf is separated and explicitly glue it to a sheaf Q.
Derive quotient local surjectivity and exact local orbit equality.
Construct D=E/Gamma and the canonical comparison E to H fiber-product_Q D.
Prove comparison locally surjective without global representatives.
Identify its injectivity precisely with testwise trivial stabilizer action.
Use the resulting isomorphism plus quotient universality to obtain the full category equivalence.
Apply the same local relation argument to nonrepresentable H_B to prove arbitrary base change.
optional_fully_proved_developments: Dense integer translations on the profinite 2-adic group give a quotient with no Hausdorff realization.
The quotient h_R/R_discrete has one ordinary point but a nontrivial negation action, showing singleton isotropy is inadequate.
likely_illicit_strengthenings: Topological orbit set is assumed to be profinite.
A locally chosen group element is assumed global.
Point values are treated as a conservative family for arbitrary sheaves.
Equivariance alone is treated as descent data for the coarse quotient.
Arbitrary base changes are assumed representable or assumed to reflect descendability.
formalization_effects: Requires new sheaf quotient, local orbit equality, internal/testwise stabilizer, and descent equivalence statements.
Pointwise set quotients or finite group-action examples alone would not formalize the general result.

public_sources.role: Profinite site and sheaf-valued condensed structures.
Local epimorphisms and effective kernel-pair quotients.
